newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria amends calculation method for lev/dlr fix.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria amends calculation method for lev/dlr fix.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said on Friday it had decided to complement its method for calculation of daily foreign currency fixings which it changed on January 6.

"If daily traded volumes for three consecutive days are below $10 million bought and $10 million sold, the BNB would calculate the lev/dollar fix on the basis of the total turnover for those days," a BNB statement said.
The new amendments were aimed at taking into account the daily movements of the lev/dollar exchange rate more precisely, a BNB official said after today's BNB board meeting.

Under the initial amendment to the method of calculation, approved on January 6, the BNB decided to change the lev/dollar fixing only if interbank volumes for the day were higher than $10 million sold and $10 million bought.
However, this led to a large disparity between the fix, which is used for accounting and statistical purposes, and the actual interbank exchange rate.

On Thursday the dollar fix was set at 731.71 levs, unchanged from Wednesday because the daily interbank turnover was below $20 million, although the market opened at 860-880 levs and closed at 890-895 levs.
The lev, under pressure due to delayed reforms and a collapsing financial system, lost 54 percent of its value against the dollar this year so far, closing at 920-930 per dollar on Friday.
Bulgaria's illiquid interbank foreign exchange market is moved by to low levels by small volumes.
